reason.text: The crm.objects.contacts.read scope allows an app to view all contacts in the user's HubSpot account, regardless of the user's own contact permissions.
reason.label: sourced

sources.quote: if a user has permissions to view only owned contacts but authorizes a request for the crm.objects.contacts.read scope, the resulting access token can view all contacts in the account and not only those owned by the authorizing user.

reason.text: The crm.objects.contacts.write scope allows an app to create contacts in the user's HubSpot account.
reason.label: sourced

sources.quote: For example, if your app required access to create contacts, you’d need to include the crm.objects.contacts.write.

reason.text: The crm.objects.custom.read scope allows an app to fetch custom object data, which is only available to Enterprise HubSpot accounts, and can be requested as an optional scope.
reason.label: sourced

sources.quote: if you want your app to be able to fetch custom object data (which is only available to Enterprise HubSpot accounts), you could add the crm.objects.custom.read scope as an optional scope.

symptom.text: The app installation fails if a conditionally required scope is included in the install URL and the user does not have access to the associated feature.
symptom.label: sourced

sources.quote: If a conditionally required scope is present in your app install URL and a user without access to the associated feature attempts to install your app using that URL, the installation will fail.

cause.text: The user does not have access to the feature associated with the conditionally required scope included in the install URL.
cause.label: sourced

sources.quote: If a conditionally required scope is present in your app install URL and a user without access to the associated feature attempts to install your app using that URL, the installation will fail.

fix.text: Provide separate install URLs for users with and without access to features requiring conditionally required scopes, omitting the scope for users without access.
fix.label: sourced

sources.quote: you could offer two install URLs to your users: one install URL could include the conditionally required scope in the scope query parameter for users with access to a feature, while another install URL omits that scope in the scope query parameter for users without access.

limits.text: If you distribute your app as private, you can install it in a maximum of 10 accounts at a time.
limits.label: sourced

sources.quote: private: used if you only want to install your app in a specific set of allowlisted accounts. If you choose this option, you can install your app in a maximum of 10 accounts at a time.
